_doc: Every destructive administrator action re-authenticates the ACTING administrator: granting admin (PATCH admin: true), creating an administrator (POST /api/admin/users with admin: true), deleting another user, issuing a reset link, resetting another user's two-step sign-in (POST /api/admin/users/{id}/mfa/reset) and the server backup (POST /api/admin/backup). They take currentPassword (422 password_required when missing, 403 wrong_password when wrong, 5 wrong tries per 15 minutes) and, from an administrator who has an authenticator, code: a current authenticator code or an unused recovery code (403 code_invalid, checked after the password, no attemptsLeft; the per-user code budget). An administrator whose only second step is the emailed code gives the password alone. Since v0.4.0 prep; before it only the backup and the two-step reset of v0.4.0 asked for the code. The two-step sign-in reset removes the target's authenticator (also a pending setup), recovery codes and email-code method, cancels open second-step challenges and pending reset links, deletes every session and revokes every personal access token (409 self_target for your own id, before the password; 404 not_found only after password and code). DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}/reset-link takes back a pending link (204). Administrator routes for users (web only in v0.4.0; the Kotlin client does not show them). AdminUser is the object of the list, create and patch answers; mfa says which second steps a user has, never a secret. lastSeenAt is null until a session was used. Every route answers 403 forbidden to a non-admin and 403 password_change_required to a restricted admin.
